title: How to Write a Brief for a Book Cover Designer
h1: How to write a brief for a book cover designer
description: Brief a book cover designer: genre, readers, title and subtitle, comparable covers, size and format, print details, files and what to ask before ordering.
intro: A book cover has to do several jobs at once: signal the genre, catch attention as a tiny thumbnail and look good on the printed book. A designer can do all of that, but only with the right information. This article explains how to write a clear brief for a book cover designer, what technical details to confirm and what to ask before you order.

faq.q: What do I need before hiring a cover designer?
faq.a: A final title and subtitle, a short description of the book, the genre and some comparable books.
Yes. Readers expect certain styles for romance, thrillers, business books and others, so the designer should know the conventions.
Print size depends on the printer, trim size and page count. Ask for exact specifications from your publishing platform.
A front cover for ebooks, a full wrap cover for print with spine and back, and a high-resolution file for marketing.

faq.q: Can I change the title later?
faq.a: Changing it after the design is expensive and may count as new work, so decide it first.
